Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the International Robotic Surgery Congress here in Orlando. Before we start, a few quick notes. The keynote begins at nine thirty in the main hall, so please take your seats a few minutes before. Coffee breaks are at ten forty-five and at three fifteen, in the exhibition area, where you can also visit the company booths. Please wear your name badge at all times. You need it to enter every session. On Thursday evening, there is a networking reception on the terrace from six to eight. It is a great chance to mingle and meet colleagues from more than forty countries. If you have any questions, the help desk is next to the main entrance. Enjoy the congress.

Hi Doctor Chen, this is Andreia Heins, the nurse from Einstein Hospital in Sao Paulo. We met at the coffee break on Thursday, near the Medtronic booth, and we talked about training programs for robotic surgery nurses. I just wanted to say it was a pleasure to meet you. I was wondering if you could send me the article about your simulation program. And do you know if your team is coming to the Latin American meeting in March? It would be great to see you there. I will send you an email today with my contact details, so we can keep in touch. Thank you, and have a good week.

Here is how Andreia networks at the congress. First, she puts on her name badge and goes to the coffee break. Then she starts a conversation with an icebreaker about the keynote. Next, she asks polite indirect questions about the other person's work. After that, she exchanges contacts with a QR code. Finally, she reaches out with a short message the next week.
